The examiner first decides the level from the chemistry, then picks the higher or lower mark in that level from how well the answer is communicated. Most questions have two or three strands (for example: do the calculation, identify the compound, explain the evidence): attempt every strand. Summary written by the site from OCR's marking instructions; being checked by our tutor.

The examiner first decides the level from how many of the question's stages are covered and how fully, then picks the higher or lower mark in that level from how well the answer is communicated. Most questions have three stages (for example: describe the method, give the observations, explain the chemistry): attempt every stage. Summary written by the site from AQA's mark schemes; being checked by our tutor.
